name: Ghost Town of Deadwood
plot: A weary bounty hunter trails a dangerous outlaw to an abandoned mining town, only to discover that the town is not empty, and the outlaws have awakened an ancient Navajo skinwalker that hunts them all.

characters.name: Narrator
characters.description: A seasoned storyteller with a heavy drawl, telling a campfire story.

characters.name: Silas Vance
characters.description: A quiet, calculating bounty hunter with a tragic past.
characters.voiceDescription: Low, tense, speaking only when necessary.

characters.name: Elias Thorne
characters.description: A vicious outlaw gang leader who fears nothing.
characters.voiceDescription: Rough, arrogant, with a manic edge.

characters.name: Nita
characters.description: A local Navajo guide who knows the legends of the canyon.

characters.name: The Skinwalker
characters.description: A shape-shifting entity mimicking sounds and voices.

dialogues.text: The wind howled through the red rock canyon, carrying the biting chill of a desert night.
Silas Vance sat by a meager fire, cleaning his Winchester rifle. Across the flames sat Nita, watching the shadows dance.
You sure the tracks lead to Deadwood?
Thorne's horses went up the ridge. Deadwood is the only thing up there. But you shouldn't follow them, bounty hunter.
There's a five hundred dollar bounty on Thorne's head. Dead or alive. I prefer dead. Less arguing on the ride back.
Deadwood is cursed ground. My people do not go there. The miners dug too deep and woke something that was sleeping.
I've faced gunmen, rustlers, and snake-oil salesmen. I'm not afraid of old ghost stories.
It is not a ghost. It wears the skin of beasts, and the voices of men. Turn back, Silas.
I need that bounty. First light, we ride.
The town of Deadwood appeared over the ridge at high noon. It was a rotting collection of wooden shacks, long abandoned to the desert.
Quiet. The horses are tied near the saloon.
The air smells wrong. Like copper and rot.
Stay here with the horses. If I'm not back in an hour, ride out.
Silas quietly unholstered his Colt revolver and kicked open the swinging doors of the Broken Spoke Saloon.
Well, well. Look what the buzzards dragged in.
Elias Thorne sat at a dusty poker table, surrounded by four of his rough-looking men, guns aimed squarely at Silas.
Party's over, Thorne. You're coming to the Marshall in Blackwater.
Are you blind, Vance? It's five against one.
I like those odds. Means I don't have to aim carefully.
Shoot him down, boys.
Before anyone could pull a trigger, a horrifying, piercing shriek echoed from outside—a sound halfway between a mountain lion and a screaming woman.
What in tarnation was that?
One of Thorne's men, Billy, stumbled through the saloon doors, bleeding profusely from his neck.
Billy! Who did this? Was it the law?
Billy collapsed onto the wooden floorboards, dead before he could answer.
That wasn't a bullet wound. Something tore his throat out.
Nita ran into the saloon, her face pale as a ghost.
It's here! The Yeenaldlooshii! The Skinwalker!
Crazy Indian talk. Someone's out there snipering my boys! Barricade the doors!
For once, Thorne, I think you should listen to her.
Outside, the wind died down. From the darkness, a voice called out.
Help me... Elias... it's Billy! I'm hurt bad...
Billy? But... Billy's dead right here on the floor!
Do not answer it! It mimics the dead to draw out the living.
Look at the window.
A monstrous silhouette leaped past the moonlight, moving incredibly fast on all fours.
Fire! Shoot it!
Thorne's men unleashed a barrage of bullets through the windows and walls, deafening everyone in the small room.
Cease fire! You're just wasting lead!
Lead won't kill it. Only silver or fire.
Silver? This is a silver mining town. The assayer's office might have unsmelted ore.
We ain't going out there! We're sitting tight till dawn!
Suddenly, the roof above them splintered, and a massive, fur-covered claw ripped one of the outlaws straight through the ceiling.
Good god!
Still want to sit tight, Thorne? Run for the mine entrance!
The survivors bolted from the saloon, sprinting across the dusty street toward the dark mouth of the silver mine.
It got another one! We're down to just me and you, Vance!
Keep moving!
They descended into the cold, damp tunnels of the mine, lighting a lantern.
Hold up. Here. A mining cart full of silver ore.
How does a rock help us against a monster?
Nita, hand me that dynamite stick from the crate. I'll pack the silver rock dust around the explosive.
A silver bomb. It might work.
From the tunnel behind them, the sound of heavy footsteps approached, followed by a twisted, gurgling voice.
Silas... Silas, come out...
It knows my name.
I ain't dying in a hole in the ground!
Thorne panicked, firing his revolver wildly into the dark tunnel. The beast lunged from the shadows, pinning Thorne to the wall.
Get it off me! Shoot it, Vance!
If I throw this, it'll kill you too!
Do it! Send me to hell, but take this thing with me!
Silas lit the fuse and threw the makeshift silver bomb directly at the beast.
Nita, get down!
The explosion rocked the mine, collapsing the tunnel entrance. A blinding flash of silver dust filled the air, followed by an unearthly, agonized scream.
When the dust settled, Thorne and the beast were gone, buried under tons of rock.
You killed it. It's truly over.
Yeah. But there goes my five hundred dollar bounty.
Silas and Nita walked out of the collapsed mine just as the sun rose, painting the desert in hues of gold.
What will you do now, Silas?
Find another bounty. Preferable one that doesn't howl at the moon.
